label: Lament_lament
translation:
At one year old, my mother died; at two years old, my father died.  
When I, Si-u-shi, was fifteen years old, my father-in-law was coming and going.  
When I got married, my sky-like father-in-law  
scolded me for being small, scolded me for being short.  
Look at my mother-in-law's walk, how hurriedly she goes out,  
scolding me for being small, scolding me for being short.  
In the men's quarters, father-in-law was sunning himself in the glass room.  
He washed his face in the washroom and ate breakfast.  
"Oh, you wicked woman, take it yourself or give it to the dog,"  
In the women's quarters, sister-in-law was sunning herself in the glass room.  
She washed her face in the washroom and ate breakfast.  
"You sly woman like a pollack, a woman who behaves like a plate,  
take it yourself or give it to the dog; such a sorrow, such a sorrow."  
I took the burden, such a sorrow, and entered the temple.  
The old monk was sleeping, the young monk was making shoes.  
"Monk, monk, great monk, please shave this child's head."  
Shaving is no problem, but the family line is noble, so it cannot be shaved.  
Although the family line is noble, please shave this child's head.  
After shaving one side of the head, thoughts of my parental home came to mind.  
After shaving the other side, thoughts of my parental home came to mind even more.  
"Monk, monk, great monk, with the 108-cord rosary around my neck,  
let's beg near my parental home, please beg, please beg.  
My daughter goes to do laundry, daughter-in-law, please beg."  
"Monk, monk, great monk, going to the bamboo grove in the forest,  
there is no one there."

Mother, mother, why did you send me out like this?  
When my mother was preparing for me to get married, she played all sorts of games, but didn't we also sing the Gomgomcho song?  
When I think deeply about Gomgom and Sansan, I feel like I can't live anymore.  
Mother, mother, whether my mother was preparing me or my mother-in-law was preparing her daughter,  
if you think about how they struck the wooden tray as if sealing water,  
there is no one who can live easily after marriage.  
Mother, mother, please take me away now.  
My love, my love, even when we sleep under the same blanket,  
you don’t understand my feelings.  
My love, my love, don't say anything about having affection just because we grew close,  
when it comes to parting, everything becomes impossible to say.  
Mother, mother, when my mother planted me, she didn’t do it lightly.  
At the end of the steep ridge, she planted me, but my roots couldn’t spread, so I feel I cannot live.  
Mother, mother,  
if in life you find it impossible to live with attachment, then clap, clap, clap your hands,  
and I will go out and live decently.  
Mother, mother,  
though all that’s left is words like a skirt,  
all that’s left is a jacket, just wearing these and holding my luggage,  
I’m going without hesitation. Mother, mother,  
if you want to see the world I’ve lived in, come into my room now.  
Though all that’s left are words like a skirt and a jacket,  
even pierced by the spaces in the field, look at me and the one I see.  
Mother, mother, my mother,  
I am leaving now, if you want to find me,  
under the thirty-six planks of the boat’s bottom, inside the small room is my room.  
Mother, mother, look at me.  
A tree laden with fruit can never have calm winds,  
and our parents, with so many children, never have a peaceful day.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The mountain is harsh and the water is harsh, words cannot be spoken, a deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river, and when I lose someone, I lose a part of myself too.  
When others lose someone, I lose someone as well. How could I not serve my husband faithfully despite this harsh fate?  
My poor husband, do not go—who will raise our young children? What sin do they bear in their youth? I just gaze up at the sky,  
thinking of my husband. When I think about it, I realized what my husband’s love truly was, but before I could fully understand, you passed away.  
How can I possibly raise this young, immature child alone? Ah, my grief…  
In this neighborhood alley, I wonder if my husband is here. Every day, whenever the sun rises, I think of my husband; even when looking at the moon, I think of him.  
I waited anxiously, hoping my husband would come home, but he has gone beyond this world. The cruel attachment remains even as I try to forget; no matter how much I steel my heart,  
your image from yesterday and today still appears vividly in my eyes.  
How could you leave me alone and go where you went?  
My in-laws complain morning and evening, my sister-in-law is troublesome, my brother-in-law is frantic,  
I carefully watch my behavior while trusting only my husband. With a single heart, I vowed to love you always,  
but why did you leave me and go beyond this world? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear.  
If I had known you were going to leave me, I would have built a fortress at the edge of the world where you went,  
If I had known it would come to this, I would have called a shaman to perform rites and exorcisms, to try to save you.  
I never imagined you would go beyond this world. They say that place beyond is better than this life; if I had known,  
every morning and evening I would have drawn holy water and prayed with my hands clasped, asking my husband not to die.  
Why did you leave me so heartlessly? Even today, I think of you. On the cold winds of winter’s end and the snow-filled solstice,  
the west winds of Bukcheongsan blow fiercely downward. That harsh winter has passed, and spring has come.  
The nightingale sings lightly and deeply, crying, and the mountains and trees—even dead wood—revive, sprouting leaves and flowers,  
but when will my departed husband come? Without a word, you torment me so.  
It is frustrating and painful; I cannot speak of it before me. A deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river.  
Coal, anthracite, bituminous coal, straw coal, bear’s fat—when burning, they produce smoke and steam, but my longing for my husband burns without any smoke or steam, only sorrow flows quietly like a droplet.  
Who understands this bruised liver? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, so dear, oh, my dear.

Mother, mother, why did my mother send me out?
There was no place to plant me, so why was I planted here?
After weeding one row, then two rows,
and two and a half rows in the Jangcheon field,
it was time for lunch.
Returning home,
I ate white porridge, then red bean porridge,
and at the end of the shelf in front of the ancestral tablet,
I wondered whether to eat or not eat that meal.
At that, the neighboring grandmother, hearing this,
said, "Chun-a, Chun-a, Okdang Chun-a, if that child belongs to the house, isn’t there a home?
If that is rice, isn’t there rice?"
Cutting and cutting off the hair, going to the temple,
hearing the neighbor’s grandmother’s words, I tore twelve pieces of cloth,
hung them up loosely, tore one piece to gather nuts,
two pieces to make a bag, and from the remaining cloth made a satin robe to wear.
Climbing the hill behind the village, the monk’s shoe strap broke,
so I asked for directions: "Please give me the way, the back gate, that way, please give me the way."
Looking along one side of the main gate, the young monk was sleeping,
the old monk did not answer, but there was also an old servant,
so I woke the young monk and told him,
"Please tie my hair, please tie my hair,
Please tie my hair tight,
If you tie it tight, at least say your name and surname."
After tying my hair into one headpiece,
the front of my hair was all wet.
After tying two bundles of hair, the front got wet with rain.
Wearing the monk’s robe, holding the wooden fish and rosary beads in my hand,
I crossed over and set out on a large road,
wearing a sky-like hat, riding a dragon-like horse,
coming along smoothly and nicely.
A person I did not know entered and stood still,
“Why? Why?”
My body felt as heavy as a thousand pounds.
“Why, monk’s robe? Why?”
"Why is this my wooden fish rosary like fire?"
Taking off the monk’s robe, I sat up, I sat up,
sat up on the embankment, sat up on the water fork embankment,
"Hurry and go, hurry and go, you must leave.
The three years of study, the studying for three years, now I am leaving after three years.
Running here and there, I can’t even run in the water."
Arriving at the gate in front of the house, the stone seat was wet,
this is the grace of the parents,
entered the room, as if asleep, gone.

translation:
Three days after marriage, I went to weed the field.
I weeded the field like the ancestral village, the field I inherited from Samsigol.
The lovebird’s tail kept circling inside the bowl of broth.
After eating this, I cannot live.
Like a three-layered comb, I shaved one side of my head.
When I shaved one side, it became like an ox beyond the ridge.
When I shaved both sides long and wide, the ridge became like a river.
That river, they say, has a pair of ducks, a pair of geese,
floating lightly.
Dressed and dressed, wearing robes and gowns,
carrying peonies,
hanging the twine,
I was about to go to Songgwangsa Temple in Suncheon to work as a monk.
The lord who was going to Seoul rode a graceful horse,
entered calmly and peacefully.
Bowing on horseback, flat and low, then he got off abruptly.
Why would a monk bow to a rider?
Dear lord, dear husband, I do not know if it could be so.
He got off the horse abruptly, then grabbed his wooden staff,
wearing a long robe made of twelve patterned panels, what kind of monk is this?
What is the silver hairpin on his head?
What is the silver ring on his wooden staff’s neckpiece?
What is an ox-hair brush on his foot?
Let’s go, let’s go, go home.
What kind of life is this to live like this?
After three years, I will go.
When I entered your house and opened your door,
all the wooden furniture and woodenware were gone.
After living three years and coming home, the yard has become a mugwort field.
I went to my father-in-law’s grave like a lantern,
lantern flowers bloom bright, broom flowers bloom bright.
At mother-in-law’s grave,
Evening primroses bloom brightly, broom flowers bloom brightly.
At my sister-in-law’s grave,
Evening primroses bloom brightly, broom flowers bloom brightly.
When I went to my husband’s grave,
Love flowers bloomed brightly, peonies bloomed brightly.
Dear lord, dear husband, after living three years, open the door.
The door opened wide, and I stepped inside.
Having sons and daughters, I lived well for a hundred generations.

Spinning wheel, spinning wheel, why is this spinning wheel here?  
Moon Ik-jeom, in the Central Plains, brought cotton seeds,  
Planted them first in Uiseong land, and it spread throughout Joseon.  
Why not use the spinning wheel to spin thread?  
Ik-jeom’s grandson made the spinning wheel,  
Marvelous and ingenious, made with great care.  
He set up two pillars, patterned after the eight trigrams,  
Selected eight bush clumps, modeled after the eight trigrams.  
Wrapped the middle string, modeled after the Yellow Path and the Red Path,  
When looking at the ear tips, the back is high and the front is low.  
The north and south roots stand firm, made following that pattern.  
Inserted the spindle, like the Big Dipper twisting,  
Attached the two ends, isn’t that the peach blossom handle?  
When spinning the long thread,  
Holding the spinning wheel in the right hand,  
Holding the cocoon in the left hand,  
Pulling long and thin strands,  
Winding around the slender body,  
The thread and the string vividly recall,  
On the seventh day of the seventh month (Chilseok), with five-colored threads,  
Is it a single thread or flowing thread? Good marital harmony.  
Wound like thread,  
Passing time without flaw,  
Let’s spin thread like silk,  
Following the heaven and earth and hell patterns,  
The yin and yang water flows skillfully.

translation:
My parents raised me with great care and affection.  
When it was time for me to join a good family, I went to live with my in-laws.  
The days were cold, the water was cold, and they told me to be careful.  
After only three days, they told me to go weed the fields.  
I refused, claiming it was a false accusation. Wearing ragged clothes,  
I held a hoe in my hand and went outside.  
There were many people at the house where I was married, so I couldn’t be seen.  
Without worry, I went outside and reached the East Sea.  
I was extremely fortunate; no matter how the winds shook from east, west, south, or north, I could not settle.  
I couldn’t distinguish right from wrong, but suddenly the workers  
chased me from all directions, saying this is my field, that is the field.  
When I crossed the field, the workers of that house followed me,  
searching the place around, hunting everywhere.  
Lightning flashed and I crossed that field.  
The front farm was my real field, and the back field was the one to be shared.  
I tried to weed by myself, and I was extremely fortunate.  
After I weeded the field alone, I weeded the rice paddies.  
I was thirsty and hungry, so I went to find Jeongshim Najal.  
Twelve people in the household had all eaten by then.  
I came to find Jeongshim Najal on account of the work.  
The old food was three-year-old barley rice,  
served in a bowl that was stained.  
The three-year-old kimchi stew was served in a dish.  
They threw food from ten miles away,  
some from five miles away, yet if I ate this rice,  
I’d choke and couldn’t swallow; I was hungry.  
I reluctantly ate the rice little by little.  
Then I saw Baekok Nangun, and when I opened the love gate and looked,  
Baekok Nangun said, “Are you leaving? Can’t you live here? Are you leaving?”  
Baekok Nangun said, “What’s this talk?  
We will live together for a thousand years; how can the parents die?”  
“Don’t go, don’t go, don’t leave me”—  
“We will live together for a thousand years; how can the parents die?”  
“Don’t go, don’t go; leave your worries and troubles behind.”  
Baekok Nangun said, “Look at my movement; bend twelve joints to support you.”  
I leaned on the wooden staff, but twelve joints broke.  
“Don’t mistake me for dead;  
although we have many partings,  
will we have more partings? This is the last word.”  
We parted with tears and I leaned on the wooden staff.  
I left the house through the gate,  
bowing deeply, walking slowly.  
As I walked, the wooden staff broke.  
Baekok Nangun ascended;  
she sat there, weeping loudly and bitterly,  
and then collapsed right there.

translation:
Mom, mom, my dear mother  
When you gave birth to me and raised me,  
Through muddy and dry places,  
Through hardships, you raised me.  
You went to the distant mountains and rivers,  
But today, there is still no news—  

Some people have good fortune—  
Living in grand, spacious houses,  
Enjoying wealth and honor—  
But why is it that I  
Live near Palgong Mountain,  
Working from dawn to dusk,  
Struggling to survive with the plants and grasses of the land,  
Carrying my burden on a shoulder pole, trying to make a living—  

Looking at the mountains and rivers, they are green hills,  
But my hair has turned white,  
How pitiful and sorrowful it is.  
My poor body is as thin as a needle,  
Afflicted with a stork-like illness,  
The one calling is my dear mother—  
The one searching is a drunken wanderer—  

At the hundred-year-old coffin by the headfield,  
Laying out the medicinal bath vessels,  
My dear, my dear beloved—  
Don’t lament that I’m leaving,  
Stay well—  

After bidding farewell at the village shrine,  
As for the path to the afterlife,  
When the gate opens, that is the journey to the other world.

Speaking in the old script, the air is silent with sorrow.  
Poor Chu Paewang, will you soon forget Chu?  
Eighteen mountains are useless; pride and power serve no purpose.  
Gripping my sword and standing up, all around are only losses.  
I wander and wander; even if I go, what can I do for you?  
Hesitating at the Three Treasures, pressing the Five Treasures,  
The superior army disperses, and my heart is scattered.  
Even the ducks of Pengsheng lament, covering their great valley,  
Heading east of the river, the defeated Paewang burns in fire.  
How can I raise my face again and see my parents anew?  
How can the people of Chu see this? Hundred generations of heroes and great men.  
Listening to the battle cry in Chu’s capital, it is all meaningless.  
Is pure heart the highest? The Han band and the hundred thousand troops  
Under the Copper Mountain, surrounding the great camp.  
When luring the sleeping Paewang, the good strategist places the mountain well.  
In the autumn night of Mount Guimyung, the jade flute laments mournfully.  
When the eight thousand disciples are scattered, that song was pure white.  
Deep in the night of Guqiu, the sky high and the moon bright,  
The wild goose cries out in the clear sky.  
It seems to stir a traveler’s sorrow, amidst the borderlands’ deadly battleground.  
Oh, soldier bidding farewell, now that your Paewang has fallen,  
War means death, and your wives and children  
In the cold wind of Hansan’s sunset, oh, how can I leave you?  
Will news come today? Will a letter come tomorrow?  
A face as beautiful as jade, a grieving husband’s deep sorrow,  
Rotting tears flow day and night.  
Placing my hand on my forehead, looking toward the departing path,  
Will I become a stone of mourning? Under Nam Mountain, constantly,  
The blowing wind, which courtesan will shield me?  
The good wine before the showdown, who will taste it?  
The son calls his father, the mother’s liver melts bend by bend.  

When General Lee Nam left, holding hands at the gate,  
Tears shed and early words spoken, leaving youthful beauty behind.  
“I will return in September next year,” a vow as firm as gold and stone.  
Firmly set in the village, “Don’t forget,” but  
Eight years of hardship have passed, and has our General Lee Nam died or lived?  
In the silent war chamber’s empty room, the loneliness of solitary mourning deepens evermore.  

– Song of Chu and Han

translation:
Frustrated, so frustrated,  
My situation is so frustrating.  
The sickle doesn’t heal, and it won’t come off,  
Carrying the carrying pole on my shoulder,  
It keeps catching on the low rocks and bumps.  
What am I to do with this miserable life?  

Some people, thanks to their parents' blessings,  
Don’t carry wood on their backs,  
They go to the village school to study,  
But my fate is miserable,  
I don’t even know how to sharpen a sickle,  
Nor do I know how to carry a load.  

When I try to carry a bundle of wood down,  
Because I’m short, the carrying pole  
Keeps catching on the rocks,  
I stumble forward,  
And the wood that I carried all falls apart.  
My heart is breaking.  

My father passed away, and under my mother’s care,  
I went to gather firewood to light a warm fire,  
But on the high mountain, while gathering wood on the way down,  
Everything fell apart. What am I to do with this miserable life?  
Oh God, what am I to do with my fate?  
I pray to God,  
Please look after this poor body of mine.  

Words:  
After living a few more years, I went to someone else’s house.  
I went to his house, and although my body was small, I carried wood.  
The strong men went ahead,  
And the weak ones like me went behind.  
But the biggest bundle of wood was only carried by the biggest man.  
When we unloaded the wood, my energy was drained.  
He carried four bundles quickly,  
While I carried two bundles and kept crying as I followed.  

A person over there  
Cannot help but cry;  
How is it that I was born into this world  
Only to suffer like this?  
The times I cried were not once or twice.  

Nowadays, I am sixty-five years old,  
Having lived through those hardships.  
I don’t complain to others,  
I live as I am,  
And that has become a mirror for me,  
When I think about it alone,  
Even now, tears flow in my bed,  
I truly live in a world that blinds me.  

The real essence of life  
Is that some people live well and some do not.  
That’s the judgment I’ve made.  
Having suffered in childhood,  
Nowadays, I think maybe I bought it with money,  
Such thoughts I’ve had about myself.  

So I wish my children,  
Unlike me, to live without suffering,  
To be ruled and guided well,  
Because I said that family teaching is very important.  
But I lost my parents early,  
While my children have both foster parents,  
Even if they suffer now,  
I will not let them suffer as I did.

Hello, folks of the military camp!  
Listen to my words:  
After departing from this world

to build the eternal home for the deceased,  
let us perform the ritual well.  
Our life, as green as spring,  
the body that just grew the day before yesterday,

The ritual sounds so lamentable,

Even the trees and grasses are sad,

Hello, everyone,  
hearing this old man's words,  
there is no such thing as eternal life.  
The remarkable founder Taejo of the Jang dynasty  
could not achieve eternal life,  
the kings of the Yi dynasty also could not.  
Jo Ja-ryong of the Three Kingdoms could not,  
and the great warlord of Shilin could not,  
Guan Yu of the Five Passes could not either,  
so how could our green life be eternal?  
Human life is destined by heaven;  
there is nothing we can do.  
Having departed from this world  
to Bukmangsan Mountain,  
if you go now, when will you come back?  
Please tell me the day you come.  
You say the mountains are high, so you can't come,  
and the waters are deep, so you can't come,  
will you come when the high peaks of Geumgangsan become plains?  
Will you come when the deep waters of the East Sea become land?  
Will you come if the red beans we planted sprout?  
Will you come if the dog boiled in the iron pot barks?  
Will you come if the green rooster in the flat plain crows loudly?  
If the mountains are too high to come,  
take it easy and climb slowly.  
If the waters are too deep to come,  
take a boat and come.  
About taking a boat,  
what kind of boat should I take?  
If I take an earthen boat,  
I fear it will fall apart, so I cannot.  
If I take a wooden boat,  
I'm afraid of the waves and can't.  
If I take an iron boat,  
I'm afraid of the magnetic compass and can't.  
If I take an earthen boat,  
it will fall apart, so can't.  
If I take a stone boat,  
I fear it will sink, so can't.  
Among these, which one?

I am afraid of the waves and can't go.  
Don't worry about the waves—  
in the time of Emperor Gaozu, General Zhuge and General Hualong were there.  
If we call General Zhuge,  
there will be no waves.  
Who will go get him?  
No one to go get him at all.  
Everything is wrong, all wrong.  
Reluctantly, we must depart,  
it's heartbreaking indeed.

listen to what I say,  
I was also young yesterday,  
but today my white hair is pitiful.

The sorrow of white hair is an enemy.  
If I had known white hair would come,  
I would have gone far away ten miles  
and built a tall fortress  
to block the coming white hair.  
We all would still be young,  
but unable to stop the white hair’s approach,

don’t boast about being the prettiest beauty in the city.  
The sun setting in the west,  
who can stop it?  
The water flowing in the East Sea,  
when will it return again?  
Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang, King Wen and Duke Zhou,  
the great sages all have passed on,  
morality has declined,

Boyi and Shuqi, who died of starvation

translation:
(Explanation)  
Kwon Sam-deuk took a fancy to going out and would sometimes be gone for a month or two. His wife, agonizing over how to feed their children at home, tightly clutched her empty stomach and wove cloth. After enduring this hardship, she prepared a knife, intending to commit suicide when her husband came home, placing the knife beside her as she wove. At that moment, her husband Kwon Sam-deuk returned. Quick-witted, noticing his wife's unusual demeanor, he leaned diagonally against the wall and playfully hit her buttocks with a weaving shuttle as he sang a song related to the loom.

(Song)  
Today, feeling bored, I shall set up the loom.  
Grasping the sky, I set the loom; catching clouds, I hang the shuttle.  
The loom’s legs are the fortress gate; its dragon-head is the three brothers.  
Playing restlessly, it reflects the lineage of our honored lord, like the royal dragon throne.  
The drum plays back and forth across Namgang River in Jinju.  
The body moves like lightning striking a narrow valley.  
The shuttle plays like rain and sun over Yong-san Mountain, splitting rainbows.  
The three dragon brothers of the carp try to catch stars or the moon, moving up and down.  
(At the end of the starter) The hand plays skillfully alone.  
Under the pillow of the chest, the threads are divided left and right.  
The shuttle plays like the royal fishing rod of our honored lord’s silver pond.  
The warp threads resemble the overwhelming troops led by our honored lord.  
Daytime weaving creates the sun’s light cloth, and nighttime weaving creates the moonlight cloth.  
It took one or two Chinese characters to weave one bolt of cloth.  
Soaked in the great silver ocean and washed in clear mountain streams,  
Hung lightly on the dragon's strings of Muju yongdam.  
The five brothers sharpen paddle-shaped mallets made of boxwood and redwood.  
Shall we try weaving the garment for our lord?  
Adding Korean needlework with Western designs,  
The silver iron slide gently presses on.  
Hung at the end of the warping beam,  
It’s boring to watch alone, but watching with two is endlessly fun.  
My wife is talented, having born a son like a crescent moon, and a daughter like a half moon,  
Weaving fine satin and silk cloth, she made a garment for my lord.  
Hurrah, long life! Hurrah, my lord!

(Explanation)  
After listening to the song, his wife was so impressed she thought, "Our man possesses such spirit," and postponed her intent to die. Later, in Seoul, a grand feast was held with ministers attending, and Kwon Sam-deuk, a master singer, was invited to perform. On a fine day in March, when he arrived at the feast, the ministers' wives were decked out in colorful makeup and vibrant clothes. Kwon Sam-deuk, playing the role of a thief, sang this song:

(Song)  
The flowers inside the hall are beautiful, but their branches are too high to reach, so I cannot pick the flowers.  
Whether I can pick them or not, let me name them.  
If I pick those flowers, they’re "sentimental flowers," but if I cannot, they’re "crabapple blossoms."

(Explanation)  
Upon hearing this, the ministers on the left side realized he was singing about their wives, and shouted to seize and imprison him. He was arrested, and a few days later, they planned to execute him, but when they brought him out, he sang the "Cow Spirit Song." He said that since he was going to die anyway, he wanted to entertain by making the ox cry once before he died and sang the song.

Having committed an offense against the lord in the Moon Palace, the fairy was cast down to the human world.  
Coming down either underground or onto the land, she found there was nothing to do at all.  
Looking around the jade railing, she saw it was empty.  
Decaying within various mountains and hills,  
She hung the pumpkin vine and saw the four legs of a loom’s frame.  
These legs are the warp and weft legs,  
The front legs raised, the back legs lowered,  
After beating the reed, she placed it against the jade railing,  
Grasping the clouds and hanging the shuttle, setting the beat to sit,  
On top sits our honored lord, as if he were seated on a dragon throne.  
Draped in brocade, as if decaying in the thick mountain ranges with waist-hung mist,  
A proud figure appearing to be the only son of three generations,  
Whether famous or fortunate, appears adorned as well.  
Moving in and out like a bear in a bamboo grove, going in and out like a blackbird laying eggs in a gooseberry field,  
Playing in and out, back and forth.  
The one called the body household is our country’s magistrate’s wife,  
As if striking a hundred times.  
The three brothers tie strings to the eyebrows of a weeping face,  
Raising and lowering a count of millions of troops with a clamor.  
Climbing up and coming down with a clatter,  
Is it the fishing spear of the lonely fisherman oppressed by the widower?  
Floating on a river of clouds.  
The three brothers are the wild women dealing with grains,  
Surrounding the cloth seller and hanging a neck at the marketplace.  
Ascending and descending, the dragon head wails.  
In the deep mountain ranges, the wild geese have lost their mates and call to them along the path.  
The iron spirits of the temple city hang their necks like the local guardian,  
Seeming like a three-year-old child twitching its limbs,  
Coming and going.  
The flying sparrow is today the sound of thunder in a sudden rainstorm.  
The sewing frame is the magistrate of our country,  
Throwing their hoe as if striking here and there.  
Day by day, two days on end, weaving a piece of cloth.  
Making silver coins and twice emptying them, moving them here and there,  
Carrying woven threads,  
Washing in the front stream with rubbing and in the back stream with rinsing,  
Neatly finishing the blue thread, what cloth were they drying?  
They were drying the robes of a scholar who had passed the state examination.  
Lighting a fire in the weltercloth, setting it beside the dragon head,  
Lowering silk bedding, carefully sewing the robe.  
Slipping it slightly into the paulownia wood bundle,  
There's news that the scholar who passed the state exam is coming.  
Stepping outside the front gate, where is the frontline battalion?  
The royal guard stands in front, accompanied by thirty soldiers.  
Reporting the situation and returning,  
Ah, how frustrating is my fate! My miserable fate!  
At the prime of youth, with a healthy body, how could I live without fragrance?  
My dear, the scholar died of thirst—  
I'll give you water, so rise up!  
He died of hunger—  
I'll give you food, so rise up!  
Refusing both food and water, I want to go to Bukmang Mountain and the fields.  
Don't bury me on the front mountain nor the back mountain.  
Bury me right in the middle of the lotus pond.  
If light rain falls, pick lotus seeds and cover me.  
If thick rain falls, pick lotus flowers and cover me.  
If a heavy downpour comes, pick lotus leaves and cover me.  
The straight tree sways and falls down with a clatter.  

-From the folk song "Yangho"

@E-e E-ehong E-hwa Neomcha E-hwahong

Among all things in heaven and earth, is there anything besides humans?  
Hey, sir, please listen to my words.  
People born into this world, it is because of your virtue that they are born.  
By the merit of Shakyamuni Buddha, borrowing the bones of your father,  
Borrowing the flesh of your mother, borrowing life from the Seven Stars,  
Praying for blessings at the Devas' altar, when my life was born,  
As a child who did not understand at one or two years old, how could I repay my parents' grace?  
The merciless years have passed, now with white hair, looking back,  
It is heartbreaking, full of grief and sorrow, so painful, so painful.  
Unable to fully repay my parents' grace, I return with white hair.  
Yesterday, youth; today, white hair—how pitiable.  
Spring grass, transient and fleeting; and royal descendants do not return.  
A human life lasts a hundred years at most, but only about forty years are lived fully.  
The body that was healthy yesterday grows sick by evening.  
Fragile and weak, suffering from a mountain-like illness,  
Calling out “Mother,” searching for her, but only cold water is there.  
Ginseng and deer antler medicines are used, but will medicine have effect?  
Calling for the only life, will compassion be granted?  
Constructing a temple on the high land, bathing in the middle chamber,  
Washing hands and feet in the lower chamber, placing a pair of candles,  
Preparing incense and the incense burner, holding the prayer paper,  
I pray, I pray, before God, I pray.  
Making vows at the Seven Stars’ altar and offering to Buddha,  
Which Buddha will be moved and respond?  
Although I go through the human world and do all acts of kindness,  
People are hungry, so I give food and gain merit for feeding,  
People are naked, so I give clothes and gain merit for supporting,  
Building temples on high mountains and places travelers pass by,  
Building houses in good places and gaining merit for sentient beings.

Time, don’t go—our lives are all growing old—if I die,

(Dialogue)  
“Ah, that tree, that tree has a lot of branches. Today, the crows are bringing lots of fortune.  
Is it going to rain now? Dark black clouds are gathering again.  
All over Hallasan mountain—huh, it really rains too often.  
Oh, over there on that ridge, there don’t seem to be many trees. Well, let’s climb one tree.”  

Hiyo—wind, strong wind, don’t blow. The west wind makes all the leaves fall, when even a big tree dies,  
the birds that used to come won’t come, and when the water becomes stagnant,  
the fish that used to come won’t come either.  
When even the flowers fall, the butterflies that used to come won’t come.  
(Dialogue)  
“Ah, over there, why are those kids climbing up like that today?  
Huh, today I have to carry a load of wood.  
Ah, so many women are coming out today, the women from Deoksan are coming up with the girls.  
What kind of mischief are they up to today, I wonder?”  

Heh—eyyo—on the mountain full of old trees—if the outside is mixed, others will know, but who knows which ones are mixed inside?  
Who would know—huh-huh-huya—huh-huh-huya.  
(Dialogue)  
“Ah, that wind is refreshing. The wind is really strong in this area.  
Spring wind or autumn wind, how refreshing it is like this.  
Women, if you go into that back valley today, you’ll find many wild greens.  
Yesterday, when I went to cut trees, there were wild greens everywhere; after that, all the women too.”  

Ehe—hihiyo—Oh-oh, Myeongsasimni, the flower of Hae-danghwa, don’t be sad because it’s withering—  
It is March of the cyclic year again—eh—oh—  
The grandmother flower on the back hill sprouted again in March of the cyclic year—  
but for people like us, why can’t we come back once we go? Why can’t we come back? It is really frustrating—ihu-huh-huya.  
Now, let’s go—ihu-huh-huya, let’s go, let’s quickly go—when my mother flew, there were twelve winding curves,  
oh, we passed every hill well.  
Ihu-huh-huya.

translation:
Three days after getting married, I was told to go weed the millet field.  
Going to weed the millet field, I found the field was as hard as stone,  
The field I was to weed was as hard as rice husks.  
I weeded one row, then two rows,  
After three or four hours of helping,  
Even though lunch was served,  
Our lunch was not brought out.  
When I went back inside the house,  
The love door (room to the in-laws) was slammed open,  
And my father-in-law said,  
"Hey, hey, daughter-in-law, how many rows did you weed in the millet field?  
Weed one row, then two rows,  
Then three or four rows again."  
"Hey, woman, go away!  
Do you call that weeding?"  
When lunch was served,  
The door to the main room was slammed open,  
And my mother-in-law said,  
"Hey, hey, daughter-in-law, how many rows did you weed in the millet field?  
Weed one row, then two rows,  
Then three rows repeatedly."  
"Hey, woman, shoo away!  
Do you call that weeding?"  
When lunch was served,  
I went into my room,  
Spread out nine panels of eaves,  
Made a hat with one panel,  
A scarf with two panels,  
A basket with four panels,  
And then I went to visit my parental home.  
Turning one corner,  
The district chief was standing there,  
"District chief, district chief, please shave my head,"  
After shaving one corner,  
Tears welled up in my eyes,  
After shaving two corners,  
Tears streamed down,  
After shaving front and back hair,  
I cried and cried.  
On that path, I arrived at my parental home,  
"Please lend me some millet,"  
Falling on the millet floor, I spilled all over the ground.  
My mother said,  
"Use the broom to sweep it away,"  
"Break the millet stalks and eat them,"  
But I am not the kind of person who eats from the tip of a broom or a millet stalk.  
"Let's eat dinner till sunset,"  
My mother said,  
"The Bodhisattva will bless us with offerings and dinner,"  
"There are cows in the stable and dogs under the floor,"  
I fell asleep in the feedroom,  
The moon was bright and the stars were bright.  
My mother said,  
"Seeing the bright moon and stars,  
You should be able to see the piece of phoenix wood,  
But if you want to see the phoenix piece,  
Look around the feedroom."  
Looking around the feedroom,  
"Child, you came?"  
They cried sadly.  
After explaining everything,  
Compassion arose naturally,  
I lived there for three or four years,  
And then went to my married home.  
At my mother-in-law's grave, chrysanthemums bloomed,  
At my father-in-law's grave, forsythias bloomed,  
At my husband's grave, hibiscus flowers waved gently in the wind.

Oh, youth of eight and twenty, do not speak ill upon seeing gray hair  
Yesterday was youth, today is white hair; what can be done about the passing time?

In the morning, the body was healthy; by evening, illness has come

The eyes once bright as the morning star, now dull—what is this?  
The face once as fair as white jade now has spiderweb cracks—what is this?  
You who once scolded so fiercely, now wear a cap—what is this?  
Even the reins that were once straight like a green ribbon—what is this?  
Oh, coral berry flower on Myungsasip-ri, the flower is falling, do not lament  
Next year in March, spring may return and you may bloom again

Praying for blessings at the shrine of God,

Praying to Jeoseok-nim with grace, and to Buddha Shakyamuni,

Can one ever repay the grace of their parents? Being born into this world,

Even if you call the shaman and hold a ritual, will the ritual work?

Oh Heo, Oh Heo, Oh Ho Neom Cha, Oh Ho,

Drying it in the sunlight, then rolling up the sharp stone spindle,

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Crow, crow, will you go to Garisan?  
Where have you been sleeping? Under the shade of Suyang Mountain.  
Here and there, under the shade, I have been sleeping.  
You have been sleeping, but as I wait for you,  
Time has passed and the day is fading away.  
What I hoped for and wished for is neither here nor there; it came but it didn’t go—nothing is certain.  
Oh, no matter what — this gentleman who hoped for and waited for me,  
Sitting under the shade, feeling good in heart and mind,  
Because it’s a cool place, I stayed and so it got late.  
Oh, no matter what — even though it’s late, as I wait for you,  
I can’t fall into a deep sleep no matter how hard I try.  
You sat, and I lay down, but when I sleep, all I do is think.  
Another day goes by and the night passes.  
Oh, no matter what — the day dawns and it’s morning,  
As I’m waiting for you,  
The sun is bright, but until that sun sets again,  
Why do you want me to wait like this?  
At night, I light the blue lantern  
And wait and wait for you to come.  
Even if the day breaks and the sun rises,  
If I turn off the blue lantern, who will be the one to do it?  
If you had come, I could have put out the light,  
But since you haven’t come,  
There is no one to put out the lantern.  
The blue lantern is brightly lit,  
If no one puts it out day and night, it just remains as it is.  
Light the fire, light the fire, light the blue lantern!  
Even the husband who was dead will come alive; the beloved who had left will return—will they?  
The lit light is in vain; no matter how much I wait, the one I hope for does not come.  
People in this world, listen:  
You cannot take what belongs to others.  
Once the moment for a person passes and they die, they do not return.  
Is there anyone who would put out the blue lantern?  
The lit flame does not go out, yet it flickers.  
If we live, we might live 500 years or so due to age,  
But when we die, we can’t extinguish even the blue lantern and die.  
— Sop'al

- Jonggeum Sae Moonseo

On a scorching hot day like fire,  
Tilling the fields like the tip of a plow,  
I worked one row, then another, when the black magpies started to caw.  
Throwing down the handle of my hoe, I turned to go home,  
Only to hear the news that my mother had died—news, oh news.  
I pulled out my hairpin and stuck it into the ground,  
Untied my ribbon and walked hanging it down,  
When I turned after a short walk, the sound of crying echoed.  
Turning a little further, the wailing of nine siblings resounded,  
The mountains, rivers, and trees trembled with the sound.  
Turning a bit more, I heard,  
“You wicked woman, a woman to be killed, why didn’t you come two days ago?”  
Oh, how suffocating my fate is,  
Tilling the fields like fire.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
It’s been thirty years since I got married, the date we met was like this.  
Was the date wrong, or was it because the year was changing? I didn’t know it would turn out this way.  
When we faced each other at the ear-splitting moment,  
Did we receive a good day? Even if we did, was the day unlucky?  
When we even untied our ear-splitting moment and met,  
We made a hundred-year promise; I didn’t know it would turn out like this.  
We endured seven years in distress and parted ways,  
I didn’t know it would be like this, even though we said we would live a hundred years.  
Who would have known it would end like this, living seven years and then parting?  
In between, we bore no fruit, nor did we sprout a single branch,  
What kind of fate is this, how can I live on? Oh, it’s so frustrating.  
I lived without knowing whether it was autumn or spring,  
The news that came was like a silent mountain, no word of the departed.  
What is there for me to live for? The water is too deep to come, the mountain is too high to climb,  
It’s so desolate like this; every night and every day,  
I counted and wished, but it was all in vain, it was all in vain.  
Where is the futility of this matter?  
Having lived without knowing the right time or season, I didn’t realize the season was passing.  
The coltsfoot flowers on the back hill resembled me, my face like a flower,  
Alone in an empty room in solitary confinement, my youth has completely faded.  
I am gone, and you survived, but shoots have sprouted and buds have blossomed,  
Even if you live well and enjoy yourself, is it because of undergarments?  
You cut short your lifespan; that field over there was fallow last year,  
This year, it’s fallow again.  
It’s become a useless field under the shade,  
It should have been sown with grains but turned out patchy.  
Now there is no ownership, even old bones come in pairs,  
And even straw sandals come in pairs; either way, it’s the same as everyone else.

Holding a sheet or a single page, I see the months of January and February with twinkling stars; in the middle of the night, the evening star is brilliant.  
Holding a sheet or a single page, I see pearls or courtesans—mothers urging us to serve our Joseon, embracing the enemy, falling into the Nakdong River.

Holding a sheet of six characters, I see Yuk Hwang, Daehwang, Seongjini teasing the eight celestial maidens.  
Holding a sheet of seven characters, I see the shadow of swallows pleasingly appearing amid the seven years’ great dullness.  
Holding a sheet of eight characters, I see the eight brothers, the sons of the brother-in-law, in Jeonju’s time; the first years of life go by easily with family affairs.  
Holding a sheet of nine characters, I see an old, tall monk wearing 108 prayer beads around his neck, grasping wrinkles with his hands, humming as he descends.  
Holding a sheet of ten characters, I see forests in Chang’an filled with tigers.  
The top hunter picks but finds nothing; the fire is deafeningly empty, and no tiger is caught.

translation:
That fallow field over there was left untilled last year,  
and this year it lies untended again.  
That fallow field lies fallow like the passing days.  
Not knowing whether it's spring or autumn, the season has slipped by,  
but the autumn flowers on the hill behind inform me.  

I went to the village where my beloved once lived,  
but the dear one is gone, unfamiliar faces and waters remain,  
the mountains, rivers, and plants grieve, the way to live is overwhelming.  

Let me look back once more at that fallow field.  
Oh, farmers who are there, please tend that fallow field.  
Hearing this, the farmers plowed it here and there,  
scattered seed grains here and there,  
from those seeds, grains sprouted and grew steadily.  

Eventually, harvest time came, and I returned.  
There is no work other than to gather that harvest.  
Doing it alone feels so lonely,  
I carefully carried the bundles and threshed them.  

I took that grain, collected it in sacks, and stored it carefully.  
In the long room of solitude, I looked again at those grains,  
picked them up, looked at them, and set them down.  
In that old fallow field, the grain was plump and fine.  

When I tried to eat those grains, I choked,  
not eating them felt unbearable.  
Spending idle days with the grain as my companion,  
countless enemies returned, my eyes darkened and ears grew deaf, becoming a stone waiting in vain.  

Go to where my beloved went, weary and sorrowful, on that distant road,  
the endless path, I will take three branches of it.  
Should I go this way or that? I lost my way.  

Suddenly, flowers appeared cluster after cluster,  
following those blooms, green mountains and clear waters prospered,  
trees and plants grew dense, plum and peach blossoms all in full bloom,  
blue and white cranes flew in, and the cuckoo cried mournfully.  

Oh birds, oh cuckoo, you and I are the same,  
why do you cry so sadly? The scenery is beautiful,  
the landscape more so.  
Singing, I entered,  
and found my lord had gone ahead,  
I hurried after him, grabbing both his wrists,  

and placed him in the immortal's hall,  
he looked at me and took comfort.  
How glad, how glad I am, after three years apart,  
the hair gray as hoarfrost, the decayed charm of manhood,  
to whom shall I show this now?  
The full autumn winds blow today.  

Oh how wonderful, oh how wonderful, so wonderful I could cry.

Among the world’s customs,  
through all eight provinces spread wide,

In Gangwon Province, the Geumgang Mountain  
is surrounded by the East Sea water.  
In Gyeonggi Province, Samgaksan Mountain  
is surrounded by the Han River.  
In Chungcheong Province, Gyeryongsan Mountain  
is surrounded by Baekmagang River.  
In Jeolla Province, Jirisan Mountain  
is surrounded by Nakdonggang River.  
In Gyeongsang Province, Taebaeksan Mountain  
is surrounded by Imjingang River.  
In Hwanghae Province, Guwolsan Mountain  
is surrounded by Mokdangang River.  

Across the wide mountains and rivers of the eight provinces,  
tracing the mountains everywhere,  
I entered these lands and landscapes.  
Looking around the universe carefully,  
I found the best auspicious place right here.  
This is the spot for my coffin to be laid.  

To the left is the Blue Dragon,  
to the right is the White Tiger.  
With Blue Dragon left and White Tiger right,  
and Nojeokbong reflected,  
this is the place for a wealthy eldest son’s coffin.  
Munpilbong watches over,  
there will be great success and passing of grand exams.  

Three days after burying this tomb,  
my father said,  
“I shall have another to be born.”  
What kind of dream did you have?  
“The Blue and Yellow Dragons twisted and rose up into the sky.”  
Ah, that dream is a great omen.  

Several months later,  
when the fetus was fully formed at ten months,  
a baby boy was born.  
The child's features were half ox,  
his demeanor like a big tree (majestic).  
At one year old, he began to speak,  
the basics of a military commander.  
At two years old, he began to walk,  
the foundation of a great general.  
By the first or second year, he could read,  
starting with the Thousand Character Classic and basic lessons for children.  
By five years old he mastered lessons,  
by eight he had comprehended  
The Four Books, Three Classics, and encyclopedias.  

When was this?  
It was early spring, the third lunar month.  
Our nation's ruler, wanting to find a wise scholar,  
visited the eight provinces.  
An exam decree was issued.  

He took down his donkey at the outskirts,  
well groomed the brushwood fire,  
prepared the pure gold saddle,  
put it on the donkey’s back.

trapping spiders in the nets,

placed foot to foot,  
pillows set properly,

Begging has come, begging has come,  
my real husband has come to beg.  
Jungjijong-a, come here,  
that woman over there is a beggar,  
don’t curse, give alms.

The examination is confusing, but what good is sighing alone in an empty room?  
Such is the fate of the four pillars of destiny, so my mind is restless.

The twisted leg is a death sentence,  
Your leg is a single leg,  
At the time of conception, there are three legs.  
The goose caught at conception walks like the male organ;  
They sit one after another.  
Generously placing a gambler’s hand with ease,  
Playing foolishly, there is no way to resist the small songs.  
Hehe, the empty sheep sits on three legs,  
Endless with silver food, the twang of the plucked bow fades,  
Is it the sound of the lone wanderer in Gyeongju?  
The cry of the dove at dawn in the clear sky,  
Crying alone as it goes.  
The crooked tree of faith hangs its neck with worn-out rope,  
Sighs when climbing up and sighs when descending.  
The three-tiered acorn cluster withers after one morning,  
Pitiful is this fate—pulling in the front water and licking in the back water,  
Spoon by spoon, it plays and unravels like the sound of children.  
Let our husband try on a real jin robe,  
I tried searching for the thread of destiny,  
Looking frantically but life, like a matchstick, inevitably departs.  
Trying to find the ear needle,  
The ears appear and then disappear.  
Picked once, picked twice, alas this is the misfortune of heaven and earth.  
It is sealed, it is sealed, the real jin robe is sealed.  
Nothing can be done, nothing can be done, my husband, nothing can be done.  
Waiting for your return in September, beneath the willow,  
The wild chrysanthemums smell sweet, but why do they bloom so late?  
Passersby each time say our gentleman has not come,  
Passersby answer that something has passed, something is lost,  
Coming down the path of the Seven Stars board.  
Hello, sir, is that true?  
Why lie?  
Losing my mind as I chase, turning at a bend,  
The twenty-eight lunar mansions march in step.  
I trusted the three generations, but the funeral time was the beginning of the curse.  
The silk skirt that was worn was the first curse,  
The straw sandals worn on black feet were also the first curse.  
In the prime of youth, unable to help but return,  
Opening the door and answering, the mandarin duck, golden bedding, and the cabinet—  
With whom are you exchanging words? My soul is gray-haired, I am dying.  
This helpless life, helpless,  
Like raw ointment, like prevention of illness.  

When the bucket drops, it falls as one,  
Listening to the cry, it mourns in a single melody.  
A feeling of one energy, one energy—this fate is one energy.  
Though youth turned to white hair, today we part and see,  
Sighs rise and anger wells up, oh, people of the clear sky,  
Hear these words:  
Having lost a head like a mountain in one day,  
Asking the soul a hundred times, it has grown restless,  
Though my body is like this, not knowing the falling flower and freezing dew, the empty sky is being emptied.  
Hello, sir, if you hear this news, please convey it to my lord:  
Why does the goose in the clear sky wander and cry along the streets?  
Thinking of this fate, goose, goose, you too came out—  
Having lost our beloved together, crossing the Han River, this is the fortune of the world.  
Namu Amitabul Gwansembosal (Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva).

On the green grass leaves, I realize,
The dew has all arrived.

Holding a stubby hoe in hand,
Wearing a tatty skirt,
And shoes attached to the skirt,
Going out to weed the field,
Whether it’s stony ground or plowed field,
Weeding one row, then two rows,
By the time the third row is done,
Looking at the land,
It seemed ink-black,
Looking at the sky,
The stars were twinkling,
Returning home and saying,
A solemn word was spoken,
“Dear daughter-in-law,
Your mother’s passed away; the news has come.”
Hearing this, “Go quickly,”
I rushed over like thunder,
Crossing a high hill,
Hearing the sound of mourning,
“How distressing, what’s this?”
At thirty-two, I was the chief mourner,
“Please stay a moment,
Let’s see your mother’s spirit briefly,” I said,
But nobody paid any attention,
She headed toward the afterlife.
When I entered my maiden home,
My sister-in-law said,
“Sister-in-law, sister-in-law,
Why are you so busy coming now?”
“Sister, sister,
Because I was living in my in-law's house,
My ears were closed for three years,
My eyes were closed for three years,
I couldn’t speak for three years,
Living like this for six years,
This is how it ended,” I said.
“Have some rice before you go,” she said,
I was served barley rice aged three years,
Ladlefuls given in a dish,
And aged soybean paste stew,
Served in a small bowl,
I was rendered speechless,
“Dog, oh dog, black dog,
You and I, eat up,
Sister, sister, my sister,
How heartless you are,
If only there had been a plate of rice,
Even if gravy remained,
I’d give you mine,
Even if the yellow radish remained,
I’d give you mine,
I’m going back to my family home.”

translation:
Three days after marriage, my sister-in-law, who picks cherries, urges me to weed the baby field.  
Look at the behavior of my mother-in-law.  
She washed her feet with cold water and urges me to weed the field.  
After weeding the first hill, then the second and third hills,  
it is almost lunchtime. As I arrive to have lunch,  
the sharp-tongued mother-in-law stirs her cold water feet.  
"Yesterday you came, my dear daughter-in-law, and today again, my dear daughter-in-law,  
what kind of work is this, coming only for lunch?"  
Hearing that voice, I was so overwhelmed that I couldn’t speak.  
Returning to my room, I tore seven pieces of cloth.  
I used two pieces to make a patchwork pouch, three pieces to make a bag,  
and one piece to make a simple sash, cutting and cutting,  
cutting my hair to look like a monk.  
I was going, but my husband said to go.  
He said he would ride a horse and go to the Seonbun family.  
Wearing half a plain sleeve, I turned around the side door.  
My husband said, "Dear, Shinjung family,  
don’t start any trouble with people.  
Dear, wearing half a plain sleeve,  
turn around the side door."  
At the end of his words, I suddenly grabbed his hand fiercely,  
trembling all over. "What’s wrong with you?  
What’s the matter with you, who usually wears a silk brocade waist bag?  
Why suddenly shave your head, who used to wear a golden hairpin and chop its hair?  
Why wear straw shoes over your worn shoes?  
Let’s go, let’s go back home."  
"I can’t go, I can’t go.  
Your parents' family is good, but I’m different, I have to go."  
Returning home, I asked my mother, "Where did he go?"  
"Since you left, he went away." The words made me so overwhelmed.  
Inside the three-foot coffin, inside the coffin, I cut my neck and died. / Sop'al

I have nothing left to do at all.”

cutting off the middle section,

The back legs were lowered,

“What else but to weave on the loom?”

playing well.

losing her beloved even at thirty,  
pushing here and there,  
her appearance is pitiful.

bent like the green and yellow dragons,  
swaying and playing well.  

The sound of the damp clay pot,  
made by splitting the jade rabbit,  
and the sounds of the millet pot being struck,  
are charming and neatly composed.  

The sound nailed down firmly—  
the drum called Buk—  
with the blue magpie sitting on its eggs,

swaying here and there, playing well.  

The grinding shuttle:  
one half here,  
the other half there.  
On the seventh day of the seventh month (Chilseok),  
the cowherd and the weaver girl cross paths.  

The playing sheep are  
the old man’s illness or not,  
trying lying down and sitting up,  
the sound of the “Won-san” song,

sounds like a lone wild goose calling for a mate.  

The naturally curved staff  
keeps going persistently,  
trying pushing and pulling.  

When weaving fine silk,  
fold the silk carefully and bind it.  
Using the silver-headed knife,  
fold the silk and bind it.  
Fold the silk and bind it.  

Boiling sweet potato starch in water,  
lift it slightly,  
put it in the front river,  
wash it in the back river,  
and using grass like jade,  
spread it on the wooden frame.  

“Let’s weave, let’s weave,  
let’s weave your clothes.”  
“What kind of clothes should I weave?”  
“Try weaving raw silk.”  

Holding silver thread in hand,  
sewing blessings with a golden needle,  
she wove your raw silk garment.  
“I have nothing left to do at all.”  

Carefully and neatly folded,  
laid it on a half-moon,  
went outside to the yard,  
and said, “Our groom must be coming.”  

He is coming,  
but is it our groom  
or not?  

“Where is your senior?”  
“Lying on the Chilseong bench, where else?”  
“What’s the matter? What’s the matter?  
What’s the matter with the Chilseong bench?”  

“I heard the Seoul rhythm is good,  
what’s the matter with the Chilseong bench?”  
“Is our senior coming?  
Is our senior coming?”  

“What’s the matter with the Chilseong bench?  
I heard the Seoul rhythm is good,  
but the Seoul rhythm is an enemy.  
If I die, there is the afterlife.  

If the gate of the afterlife is like a door,  
if it opens and closes, won’t I go through it?  
If the path to the afterlife is like a road,  
even coming and going, won’t I be able to go?  
It’s the enemy, it’s the enemy,  
the Seoul rhythm is the enemy.”

Copper boiled in the mist, to sit here or not to sit?  
The seated fairy is like a narcissus flower and gentle.  
Treading on the waistboard, the sheep wrapped around the waist

The talking sheep is the only son of three generations, the only child.  
Alas, the night farmer has gone; in the early dawn frost and cold wind  
The wild geese lost their mate and wail like the sound of parting friends.  
The old woman with beans seems to have fallen ill.  
Sitting or lying down, no action brings improvement.  
Is it a disease without a cure? Shaking this way and that way.  
The wild geese crying in the early dawn frost and cold wind,  
If you go to where my lord resides,  
Please convey my regards.

I am crying and searching, but I do not know where he is.  

Thump, thump, thumping, jumping over,  
The firewood logs on Bonggil beach, weaving all silken cloth.

Empty with gold thread, sewing with silver needles,

Gradually fining and organizing, half-closing the door,

Neatly setting it up, neatly setting it up,

Lying on the North Star board, what does this mean? What is this meaning?

Did you die on a mountain road? Did you die of thirst?  
Come up and see the water. Did you die from hunger?  
Come up and see the rice. If you die because of me,  
Come and see me. How is the road to the afterlife?

Wearing crooked shoes on worn feet, why say such things?  
In hands that once wore a gold watch, why this sorrow?  
Oh, so painful and suffocating, carrying a bundle on my back,  
Feet, save me, I will seek my love and live.

Mother-in-law's words:
She told me to weed the field like a huge plain.
With a wooden hoe in hand,
Weeding one row, weeding two rows,
Weeding three rows, I found
The scorching hot sun
Was like the vast plain.
Weeding this row and that row,
By the time I finished, it was noon.
Throwing down the wooden hoe,
I went inside the house,
And mother-in-law said:
"Why did you come back without weeding your feet?"
Weeding three rows of the vast field,
By the time it was noon,
I came to eat lunch.
Oh, that woman has a strong appetite,
She knows what hunger is.
The vast field
Had not even been half weeded.
Hearing that, I turned back,
Took off my shoes and held them beside me,
Steadily trudging up the mountain path.
The black crow cawed loudly,
"Obituary, obituary!
News of my mother-in-law’s passing."
The right hand received the news,
The left hand grieved,
My mother-in-law had passed away.
Slipping my shoes back on,
Steadily following the path,
But there was no sign of where mother had gone,
My mind was in turmoil.
Having missed lunch,
Is this all a young woman is for?
This is enough of living with an in-law,
Let's stop once more and go somewhere,
To deep water like the Han River,
Dressed in a funeral dress like a lotus flower,
Diving in to die,
Who would care?
The rough willow branches were stirred,
Grabbing a willow branch,
I asked sharply,
"Didn't that young master leave without reason?
There’s no way he would die like that."
I thought again,
Follow me with this hand,
Grasping the young master's hand,
Crossing one ridge lovingly, then the second,
Passing the third,
Coming to a house like an uncle's,
Where a flower garden spread out and sat playing.
This much is living,
It's not like dying and never seeing again.
Meeting that young master,
We made a hundred-year vow,
Had a son and a daughter,
And my life was enriched and continued,
I was born anew.

translation:
Three days after getting married, what my mother-in-law said:

Where have you been, my daughter-in-law? Where have you been, my daughter-in-law?  
Do you want to weed the field or the rice paddy? The field need not be weeded,  
but how can the rice paddy be weeded? She said, "Follow the dog."  
So I followed the dog and found it had gone to the field.  
Weeding one row, then two rows,  
my finger that once wore a silver ring,  
why now is it tied with hemp string?  
The silk apron I once wore,  
why now is it a cotton apron?  
The floral shoes I used to wear,  
why now are they woven from straw?  
When I looked around carefully,  
as evening came,  
no matter how many rows I weeded—one row, two rows, three rows—  
all other hearts may have come out,  
but my heart does not come out.  

When I went inside the house,  
the front and middle doors were all locked.  
"Sister-in-law, open the door!  
I’ve been weeding the fields," I said.  
In the scorching sun of a cold day,  
no matter how many rows I weeded—one row, two rows, three rows—  
all other hearts may have come out,  
but my heart does not come out.  

"Go away, you wretched woman!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you looking for the right time and day?"  
This is what my father-in-law said.  

"Go away, you wretched woman!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you looking for the right time and day?"  
My mother-in-law said sharply:  
"Go rot away in your own house!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you waiting for the right day and time?"  

Crossing the southern hill with determination,  
she dipped the rice she ate the night before  
into a bowl of soup,  
and wiped the crumbs of three years’ worth of meals  
onto a small dish.  
Feeling sorry and downhearted,  
she ate those all up,  
then entered my room.  

She took nine pieces of the widow’s dress—  
carefully unfolded each layer—  
one piece was torn,  
one piece was shaped into a cone,  
one piece was finely cut,  
and when one roll was spun round and round,  
my husband who had gone to Seoul came down  
wearing a hat like the heavens,  
riding a horse above the attic,  
and dismounting with a bang.  

Startled, I said:  
“Hold my wrists tightly,  
hey, you! Hey, you!  
Where are you going? Where are you going?  
I can’t live anymore,  
I can’t live in your house.  
Your parents are frightening,  
your younger siblings are frightening.  
Their parents always demand 'buy me',  
and your siblings also keep demanding 'buy me'.  
Come with me, come with me!  
I just can’t live here, I just can’t live here!”  

When one turn of the roll went by,  
a friend came out and called,  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
cut my hair, please.”  
After she cut one side of my hair,  
the dew started to fall naturally,  
after shaving the double braids,  
a great wailing naturally arose.  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
let’s go begging at my maternal home.”  

Entering the gate of my parental home,  
“Please give me alms, please give me alms.”  
My eldest son-in-law cursed,  
“Among these people, some look like our sister-in-law.”  
“I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike.”  
“Should I give you glutinous rice liquor or non-glutinous rice liquor?  
I throw away the glutinous and non-glutinous rice,  
please give me millet.”  
I gather millet endlessly in a bottomless pit until sunset.  

My sibling, going to the village school,  
said, “Among these people, some resemble our elder sister.”  
“I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike.”  
My mother is ill,  
and some resemble my daughter.  
"I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike."  

As the day ended,  
I thought I’d stay a while in this house,  
but there was no room, so I couldn’t sleep.  
Trying to sleep under the floor,  
I sat there but couldn’t sleep because worries came flooding.  
It was almost midnight.  

“Mother, mother, my mother,  
I didn't realize this was how it would be.”  
I repeatedly knocked on the three doors,  
when my mother opened the door,  
she cursed loudly,  
and clasping both hands together,  
she wailed loudly.  

As day broke,  
I went around with my friend,  
traveling north, south, east, and west.  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
let’s go begging at my marital home.”  

When I went begging at my marital home,  
at my father-in-law’s grave, the dragon’s spirit flower bloomed,  
at my mother-in-law’s grave, the wild grass flower bloomed,  
and at my husband’s grave, the hibiscus flower bloomed.  

Looking around my house,  
the hemp field had become untended.  
“Let me split it, let me split it,  
hey, you! Hey, you!  
Let me split just half,  
let’s try living in the afterlife.”  
When splitting half,  
he entered that grave.
